items.rationale: Sections 2.4.2 and 7.1.7(h) cover necessary cleaning of the directly wetted floor. The estimate allows €65 gross for a small affected area, not a general room clean.
The hallway was directly wetted, so necessary residue removal is covered under 7.1.7(h). Allow €80 gross for the larger affected area, in line with the cleaning allowance in Case 21.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers checking the source and confirming that leakage has stopped, even if the appliance itself is not insured. Allow €85 gross for a basic check without appliance repair.

items.description: Remove and dispose of damaged skirting
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.7(a) and 5.2.1 allow removal and disposal of damaged fixed trim. Allow €100 gross for removal and disposal of a small quantity across the two affected areas.
Sections 7.1.5, 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 limit replacement to damaged lengths at the pre-loss specification. Allow €220 gross for ordinary matching skirting, fixings and fitting.

items.description: Clean and repaint unaffected upstairs bedroom
items.rationale: Sections 3.5 and 7.1.5 exclude both tasks because the upstairs bedroom was not reached by the water. No part of the combined line is attributable to the leak.

items.description: Measure moisture in utility room and hallway
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(b) covers moisture measurements in both affected rooms. Allow €165 gross for the combined survey, consistent with Case 21, without duplicating separately billed labour.

Section 7.1.7(b) covers necessary drying in the affected spaces. Allow €105 gross for the drying service apart from separately billed rental and labour, subject to the duplicate-charge exclusion in 7.1.8(c).
Section 7.1.7(e) covers necessary drying equipment hire, provided it is not already included in the drying charge. Allow €50 gross for one modest rental, in line with Case 21.

Section 7.1.7(g) covers separately identifiable labour on the affected areas, but 7.1.8(c) excludes duplicate charges and 7.1.5 excludes basement work. Four eligible hours at €47 gross per hour give €188.

items.description: Measure and dry unaffected basement storage room
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) exclude measurement and drying in a separate room with no documented damage. Neither part of the combined line qualifies.

Section 5.2.6 covers specialist transport only from the balance of the €1,190 gross per-item cap after restoration. Full restoration is estimated to exhaust the cap; if a balance remains, allow up to €85 gross for this first ancillary line.
The assessment is required by 5.2.6, but its cost is paid only from any cap balance left after restoration and transport. If enough remains for a payment, estimate €115 gross.
Section 5.2.6 covers specialist drying and stabilisation, but this line ranks behind restoration, transport and assessment under the shared cap. If a balance reaches this line, estimate €150 gross.

Under 5.2.6, restoration has first claim on the single cap for this unscheduled painting. The specialist restoration is estimated to reach the cap of €1,000 net × 1.19 = €1,190 gross, assuming VAT was incurred and is not recoverable under 7.7.
Section 5.2.6 applies only to an item affected by the insured event. The second painting was unaffected and does not qualify for a separate conservation allowance.
Section 7.1.8(b) excludes separate administrative, handling and processing fees. This is also outside the specialist conservation measures listed in 5.2.6.
